newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bank raising capital of two mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bank raising capital of two mutual funds.

text.p: The National Bank of Egypt and National Fund Management Company said on Sunday they were raising the capital of their two mutual funds by offering units in each fund worth 100 million pounds ($29 million).
In a published advertisement, the state-owned bank and company said they wanted to increase the capital of their accumulative fund to 200 million pounds from 100 million.
The capital of the second fund, which gives regular payouts, would rise to 300 million pounds from the current 200 million, the advertisement said.
The price of the accumulative fund unit is 801.25 pounds and units of the other fund are priced at 118.5 pounds each, a bank official said.
The bank and firm set up the accumulative fund, the country's first, in 1995. A few months later they set up the other fund which is aimed at smaller investors and pays a dividend every three months.
The advertisment said the accumulative fund made a 33.4 percent gain on investments in 1996 while the other fund made a 29.6 percent gain.
Several other banks and a few institutions have set up similar mutual funds in the last three years.
